title: Stoicism & Modern Life
rootClaim: Stoicism provides an optimal practical philosophy for modern psychological resilience, emotional mastery, and virtuous living.

branches.text: Dichotomy of Control: Focusing exclusively on what is within internal agency while accepting external events removes anxiety and cultivates tranquility (Ataraxia).

children.text: Foundation of Modern CBT: Albert Ellis and Aaron Beck developed Cognitive Behavioral Therapy directly from Stoic principles (epictetus: 'People are disturbed not by things, but by the view they take of them').
Emotional Repression & Detachment Critique: Misapplication of Stoicism encourages suppression of authentic grief and emotional vulnerability ('broic' toxic apathy).

Propatheiai Distinction: Ancient Stoicism explicitly distinguishes between automatic initial emotional impressions (propatheiai) and rational assent, encouraging emotional processing rather than denial.
Passivism in Systemic Justice: Over-emphasizing internal acceptance risks discouraging collective political resistance against external societal oppression.
Amor Fati & Memento Mori: Embracing fate and keeping mortality salient deepens daily gratitude, courage, and purpose.

branches.text: Modern Critique of Stoic Physics & Virtue Monism: Stoicism relies on outdated Teleological Cosmology (Cosmic Logos) that modern secular science invalidates.

children.text: Loss of Cosmological Grounding: Ancient Stoics justified accepting fate because the universe was a providential, rational organism; modern random evolutionary biology undermines this providence.
Modern Secular Stoicism (Pigliucci, Sellars): Stoic ethics and cognitive strategies function effectively as practical heuristics independently of ancient cosmological physics.

definitions.description: The fundamental Stoic principle dividing all things into what is up to us (our thoughts, desires, actions) and what is not up to us (external events, outcomes, opinions of others).
A state of serene calmness, untroubled mind, and freedom from emotional disturbance.
The philosophical attitude of active acceptance and enthusiasm toward everything that happens in one's life, including suffering and adversity.
In Stoic psychology, the involuntary physical and emotional proto-passions that occur before conscious reflection and rational assent.
The ancient Stoic belief in a rational, divine principle governing and animating the order of the cosmos.
